changes.before: IGN reports, citing the Japanese outlet GameBiz, that at its Capcom Open Conference RE: 2026 on 2 Oct 2026 programmer Satoshi Ishida laid out the REX project, a step-by-step upgrade of the Resident Evil maker's RE Engine aimed at making it an AI-generation game engine where staff "create games together with AI". changes.after: IGN reports, citing the Japanese outlet GameBiz, that at its Capcom Open Conference RE: 2026 on 2 Oct 2026 programmer Satoshi Ishida laid out the REX project, a step-by-step upgrade of the Resident Evil maker's RE Engine aimed at making it an AI-generation game engine where staff "create games together with AI". changes.before: Microsoft has released a test that judges AI agents by the database records they leave behind and finds most models cannot repeat a success twenty times.

changes.reason: 'most models cannot repeat a success twenty times' was a loose generalisation; the facts give the best model passing 241 of 507 tasks on all 20 tries.

changes.before: Microsoft's Copilot Studio team writes on Hugging Face that it has released ThinkingBox, a sandbox and benchmark of 507 synthetic business workflows that grades an AI agent on the final state of the backend database rather than on its replies, running every task 20 times; across 12 models about two thirds of failed attempts ended cleanly with no error reported while leaving wrong values behind. In Microsoft's figures Claude Opus 5.5 leads single-attempt success at 67 percent, Kimi-K3 solves 94 percent of tasks at least once but only 13 percent every time, and the team says about four in five failures are tool handling rather than reasoning.
changes.after: Microsoft's Copilot Studio team writes on Hugging Face that it has released ThinkingBox, a sandbox and benchmark of 507 synthetic business workflows that grades an AI agent on the final state of the backend database rather than on its replies, running every task 20 times; across 12 models about two thirds of failed attempts ended with no error reported, and most of those left wrong values in the records. In Microsoft's figures Claude Opus 5.5 leads single-attempt success at 67 percent, Kimi-K3 solves 94 percent of tasks at least once but only 13 percent every time, and the team says about four in five failures are tool handling rather than reasoning.
changes.reason: Two separate figures (67% silent failures; 78% of those with wrong values) were merged into one claim; separated them as the facts state.
